newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic/Somnus to develop sleep disorder therapy.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic/Somnus to develop sleep disorder therapy.

text.p: Medtronic Inc and Somnus Medical Technologies Inc said Tuesday they agreed to jointly develop a non-invasive therapy for sleep disorders, including snoring and sleep apnea.
Medtronic has made a minority investment in Somnus and gained exclusive distribution rights in Europe and certain Pacific Rim countries, according to a joint statement.

Snoring occurs when tissues in the upper airway relax during sleep and partially block airflow through passages in the back of the mouth, nose and throat. About 40 million people in the United States suffer from habitual snoring.

In obstructive sleep apnea, tissues of the upper airway relax during sleep and restrict breathing. Sufferers arouse frequently to avoid suffocation and, as a result, experience severe sleep deprivation over time. About 70 million people worldwide, including more than 20 million Americans of whom only about 400,000 have been treated.
Somnus has a system which opens airway passages without the swelling and bleeding associated with surgical therapies.
Medtronic and Somnus will co-manage European clinical testing and submit data seeking marketing clearance for the system.
Medtronic has developed a system to control sleep apnea. It is now in clinical trials in the United States and Europe.
Somnus, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., is a privately held company which developed the treatment for snoring.
